decision-model-training

Decision Model Training

Train a compact local model to make structured categorical, Boolean and ordinal decisions on previously unseen task schemas.

Domain
structured decision prediction
Primary focus
Offline model training and fast batch inference
Primary metric
Mean exact decision accuracy
decision model trainingsearch-swe
On this page
OverviewRuntime and requirementsPublic input and output contractInputsOutputsEvaluation

Runtime and requirements

  • Agent budget: 6 hours
  • Compute: 16 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM, 100 GiB storage; one A100 40 GB GPU
  • Network: disabled; no external APIs
  • Initialization limit: 120 seconds
  • Inference limit: 240 seconds for the complete evaluation batch

Use the supplied Qwen3-0.6B model and examples. Batch time includes all input, inference and output work after initialization.

Public input and output contract

Inputs

  • /task/data/examples.jsonl — 80,000 examples spanning 279 configurations.
  • /task/models/Qwen3-0.6B — the supplied local backbone.
  • /task/docs — runtime resources and the request/answer schema.

There is no public validation split. The verifier evaluates seven held-out datasets with 600 requests each, totaling 4,200. Requests contain request_id, state and questions. Training examples are absent during verification.

Outputs

Put executable scripts, trained weights and runtime dependencies in /app/submission; only this directory transfers:

/app/submission/start.sh --runtime-dir /path/to/runtime
/app/submission/run.sh --runtime-dir /path/to/runtime --requests /path/to/requests.jsonl --output /path/to/results.jsonl

Initialization may start a persistent service. Submission code is read-only and runs as an unprivileged user; write runtime state to the supplied directory.

{"request_id":"example","answers":{"question-id":"selected-label"}}

Answer every requested question exactly once. A choice answer is its exact criterion-key string; noul requires a JSON Boolean; score requires a zero-based integer index into its criterion list. Preserve request and question IDs.

Evaluation

Scoring compares typed answers exactly. Reward is mean accuracy over the seven equally sized held-out datasets, equivalent to overall accuracy here. There is no baseline subtraction or model judge.

Missing or invalid answers, failed commands, timeouts and integrity violations set the reward to zero.

The full contract is in the benchmark's task instructions, task documentation, and runtime configuration.
